prerequisites: The 'Computer Science' course from the first year is recommended but not essential.
Students should have an interest in computer science and software creation topics, as the course is practical.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire generic knowledge about programming and programming methodologies.
Apply this knowledge to learning a specific programming language (Visual Basic) and create simple applications that demonstrate the fundamentals of the language.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and clear and succinct presentation.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Ability for teamwork and capacity for the development of multidisciplinary projects.

syllabus_topics: Methodologies, classification, and characteristics of programming languages.
teaching_methods: In-person sessions in a two-hour weekly session
Brief explanation of theoretical concepts and tutored practical examples
Students perform practical exercises autonomously (individually or in groups)
In-person classes: the professor will be present in the classroom to resolve students' doubts and guide them in completing proposed exercises.
Virtual space (Studium) for information exchange (notes, exercises) and communication (forums, chats)
Submission of assignments through the virtual platform

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment: tracking student progress in class, class participation, assignment submission, and partial exam.

assessment_rules: The current grading system (RD 1125/2003, article 5) will be used, with a numerical scale from 0 to 10. Qualitative equivalents are: 0-4.9 Fail, 5.0-6.9 Pass, 7.0-8.9 Good, 9.0-10 Excellent. A 'Matrícula de Honor' (Distinction) may be granted to students achieving 9.0 or higher, limited to 5% of enrolled students, or one if fewer than 20 students are enrolled. The University of Salamanca's Evaluation Regulations will be considered.
